name: stagger-text
title: Stagger Text
author: HoverUI (https://hoverui.com)
description: Letters lift in a 35ms wavefront, so the word reads as a row of keys going down in sequence. The word stays fully set and legible at every frame — nothing fades in or arrives. Nothing ships to the client: it is a server component with no hooks and no handlers, and the whole effect is CSS. Text is not focusable, so it answers any focusable ancestor's :focus-visible as well as its own hover; text with no interactive ancestor has no keyboard state, by design. Under reduced motion it does nothing — the lift is decoration over an already-readable word, and dimming it would drop below AA contrast. Note: the text is split into per-grapheme boxes, which suspends kerning and ligatures across each word, and the string appears twice in the DOM — once for assistive technology, once split and hidden from it.
